name: N-Acetyl Selank Amidate

lead: N-Acetyl Selank Amidate is a chemically modified version of the peptide Selank, with changes meant to help it resist breakdown and last longer in the body. Users hope for a calmer mood and more social ease than the parent peptide gives.

The chain is indirect: less anxiety and stress, a calmer and more composed demeanour, and better social presence. It is presumed to act like Selank, which is described as modulating GABAergic signalling. No studies of this exact compound are reported, and the benefits are extrapolated from Selank research.

paras: It is sold by research-chemical suppliers for laboratory use. Users describe it as a longer-lasting alternative to Selank, with no established routine or timeline.
It is not approved for human use in most jurisdictions. Safety in people has not been studied.

angle.text: This acetylated, amidated Selank analogue is sold as a research chemical, with users hoping for less anxiety, a calmer demeanour and more social ease. The link to looks runs through composure and presence. The analogue itself has no direct studies; the research relates to Selank.

lead: N-Acetyl Selank Amidate is a synthetic heptapeptide analog of Selank, with the sequence Ac-Thr-Lys-Pro-Arg-Pro-Gly-Pro-NH2, N-terminally acetylated and C-terminally amidated. These changes are described as intended to resist enzymatic breakdown. [1]

It is sold by research-chemical suppliers for laboratory use and is not approved for human therapeutic use. Claimed benefits are extrapolated from Selank research; the source reports no direct studies of this variant. [1]

paras: The acetyl group at the N-terminus is described as blocking aminopeptidases, and the amide at the C-terminus as blocking carboxypeptidases. [1] The stability benefits are described as hypothesized and unverified for this specific compound. [1]
No studies found. Any clinical or animal findings relate to unmodified Selank, not this variant. [1]
